ask: Go 1.22. pipeline.go: channel pipeline — generator, fan-out to N transformers, fan-in with WaitGroup, context cancellation propagated to every stage, bounded buffers, error channel with errgroup-free collection, and a main that runs it with a timeout. write the file.
prose:
Wrote `pipeline.go` with the full pipeline. Here's the shape of it:

- `generate` — single goroutine emits `Item`s on a buffered channel, selects on `ctx.Done()` so cancellation stops production and closes the channel.
- `fanOut` — spawns N worker goroutines, each with its own buffered result channel, all reading from the shared source channel. Go's channel semantics handle the multiplexing safely since only one worker receives each item.
- `transform` — per worker, reads items, calls `process` (which doubles the value and errors on `value == 42` to demonstrate non-fatal error propagation), sends a `Result` that carries either the item or the error.
- `fanIn` — merges the N result channels into one using a `sync.WaitGroup`; each forwarder goroutine drains its input channel into the merged channel, and a separate goroutine waits on the WG to close `merged` only after all forwarders finish.
- `collect` — drains the merged channel synchronously, splitting results into `items` and `errs` slices. No `errgroup` involved.
- `main` — wires it with `context.WithTimeout` (2s), runs `collect`, then prints processed items, errors, and whether the deadline fired.

Build and run:

```bash
go mod init pipeline 2>/dev/null
go run pipeline.go
```

The bounded buffers (16 on the generator, 8 per worker, 32 on the merged channel) give backpressure without unbounded growth. Cancellation propagates at every send and receive via the `select` on `ctx.Done()`, so a timeout tears down all stages cleanly.
